author.name: E. Nesbit
author.biography: Edith Nesbit wrote The Railway Children and Five Children and It, and was a founding member of the Fabian Society.

hook.text: What is left of Shakespeare when his plays are told as stories?

paragraphs: Twenty of Shakespeare's plays, each told as a short story: comedies such as A Midsummer Night's Dream, Twelfth Night and Much Ado About Nothing, tragedies such as Hamlet, Macbeth, King Lear and Othello, and late plays such as The Tempest and The Winter's Tale.

Each story follows its play's plot from beginning to end with the main characters in place, and turns most of the speeches into plain narration. The comedies keep their twists: twins mistaken for each other, lost children found, and young women in disguise as young men.
Use it as a first meeting with a play before you read or see it, or as a reminder of who is who afterwards. The stories tell each play to its own ending, happy or not.
The volume opens with a preface in praise of Shakespeare and a short life of him that begins with his baptism in the parish register at Stratford-upon-Avon in 1564.

orientation.text: Twenty-two chapters: the preface, the life of Shakespeare, and one story for each play. Every story stands alone, so start with any play you are curious about.
